The haqq relayer (packets and ICQ responses) stays off until the upgrade; do not relay haqq's packets 85-98 or their timeouts (§9c).

steps.text: Channels tab: every in-scope ICA channel OPEN (haqq's delegation and withdrawal channels are the known closed ones), no pending packets, every client live; Pre-flight checks all ok, including Band's host client of Stride.

No unacked ICA packet on any zone except the known ones (haqq's closed channel-869, Juno's channel-491 if not cleared): the v35 reset only clears DelegationChangesInProgress on a zone whose delegation channel is open with no unacked packet, so expect the Hub reset and a logged skip for juno-1 and haqq.

Everyone for upgrade day confirmed: haqq relayer operator, protocol admin signers, staketia operator, stakedym operator, Osmosis vault signers.

days.title: Upgrade day
days.note: Haqq first: its sequence through 1f must finish before 19:00 UTC, haqq's unbonding epoch, or its queued records and drain move to 10-16. The spec orders every other zone's refresh after the haqq sequence; because both must finish by 19:00 UTC, the other zones start once the haqq restore (1d) is in flight, and never before 1b.
avoid: Do not relay timeouts for haqq packets 85-98: the restore zeroes their flags and a timeout processed afterwards errors in DecrementValidatorDelegationChangesInProgress (§9 step 1c).

Do not submit drain batches between about 14:12 and 19:00 UTC: the batch's ICA timeout is the next day-epoch start minus a fifth of the epoch, so in that window it is already in the past and a lagging light client can let the packet out, time it out at once and close the ordered delegation channel (§9 step 4).

When clearing a zone's undelegate packets, relay acknowledgements before timeouts and never relay a timeout while an earlier sequence's ack is outstanding: a timeout that closes the channel first leaves executed batches unacknowledged and Stride still recording their delegations (§9 step 4).

Do not MsgTransferFromIca the DELEGATION or REDEMPTION ICA of a zone yet: the delegation ICA receives the unbonded records and the redemption ICA holds claimable tokens until every claim is paid (§9 steps 5-6).
Do not run update-delegation or calibrate-delegation on other zones before haqq's channel-29 is closed and its restore is in flight; haqq goes first (§9 step 1).

steps.text: v35 executes and the chain resumes. Read the v35: logs: the haqq delta table applied (which rows, if any, were skipped on a stale pin), stale DelegationChangesInProgress reset on every zone whose delegation channel is open with no unacked packet (a logged skip for juno-1 and haqq is expected unless Juno was cleared), ICQ purges, rate limits removed, wasm control to gov, comdex deprecated, oracles deactivated.
Turn the haqq relayer on (packets and ICQ responses).
Stop the Neutron and Carbon relayer pairs (their Stride leg is not needed after the upgrade; the relayer scope table decides their Osmosis legs).
Record each zone's RedemptionRate at the upgrade height (the pools' rate; nothing moves it afterwards).

Confirm the upgrade's haqq work: the delta table applied, not skipped; no haqq slash-path query remains; no haqq validator has SlashQueryInProgress. If the whole table was skipped (a missing validator), stop and decide by hand before restoring.

Close haqq's channel-29: the relayer submits MsgChannelCloseConfirm on haqq for icahost/channel-29, proving channel-869 CLOSED on Stride (needs haqq's client of Stride Active). Verify channel-29 CLOSED on haqq.

Verify: Channels tab shows the new delegation channel OPEN on both ends; HostZone.DelegationIcaAddress unchanged; Validators tab → haqq: every validator at Δ in progress 0; Funds tab → haqq Records column still shows the 2 queued records.

Done when the Channels tab shows a new haqq DELEGATION channel OPEN on both ends and the Validators tab shows every haqq validator at Δ in progress 0. If the handshake stalls, check haqq's client of Stride (Channels tab: haqq host client) and the relayer's client updates.

steps.expect: code: 0; done when the Channels tab shows a new haqq WITHDRAWAL channel OPEN on both ends.

steps.text: Prove an ICQ round trip: update-delegation for one haqq validator; Validators tab → haqq: its 'slash query' pill turns on, then off, and its rate diff goes to 0. If the second callback keeps timing out, fix the relayer (frequent client updates toward Stride) before 1f.

steps.expect: code: 0; then on the Validators tab → haqq the validator's 'slash query' pill turns on (the rate callback landed and submitted the shares query) and back off (the shares callback landed). If it stays on for more than an hour the ICQ is timing out: fix the relayer's client updates toward Stride before 1f.

for V in $(curl -s -A curl/8.0 https://stride-strd-api.polkachu.com/Stride-Labs/stride/stakeibc/host_zone/haqq_11235-1 | jq -r '.host_zone.validators[].address'); do strided tx stakeibc update-delegation haqq_11235-1 $V --from <PROTOCOL_ADMIN_KEY> --chain-id stride-1 --node https://stride-strd-rpc.polkachu.com:443 --gas auto --gas-adjustment 1.5 -y; done

Then RESULT: PASS for haqq with no --allow-over: after the refresh haqq must be clean. On FAIL, the named validators need calibrate-delegation; wait for the callbacks and rerun.

steps.expect: Every update-delegation lands with code: 0 (one tx per validator; sequence them or use --sequence). Then the drift script: RESULT: PASS for every zone. On FAIL, the verdict names the zone and validator: calibrate-delegation when the rate is unchanged but the balance is off (strided tx stakeibc calibrate-delegation <CHAIN_ID> <VALOPER>); wait for the callback (Validators tab: slash query pill off) and rerun.

The staketia operator undelegates the remaining multisig delegation on Celestia via authz, in one go (69.4B utia on 2026-10-05: the 87.43B behind records 1472-1488 was already undelegated on 2026-10-05 and completes 2026-10-19 22:45 UTC).

Record each pool's id and rate_at_creation in the CONSTANTS of scripts/wind-down/check_transmuter_pool.py and build the pools.json that scripts/wind-down/coverage_check.py --pools reads; neither script runs without them.

steps.expect: After adding each new pool's id and rate_at_creation to the CONSTANTS block: RESULT: PASS for every pool (the 'host zone is not halted' warning disappears once the rate is frozen). On FAIL, fix the pool (add_new_assets / roles) or the CONSTANTS entry and rerun before funding anything.

steps.text: The day epoch submits the queued redemptions on every zone (1500 is divisible by every unbonding frequency) and flags their validators; wait for the acks (Channels tab: delegation channels back to 0 pending; Validators tab: Δ in progress back to 0). Funds tab → Records: a record that stays in UNBONDING_RETRY_QUEUE failed (a slash between the refresh and the epoch) and is retried at the zone's next unbonding epoch; that zone's drain waits.
Haqq's epoch submits its two queued records (epochs 1487 and 1488); wait for the acks over haqq's slow blocks, then drain haqq like the other zones.

Per zone: MsgUndelegateFromValidators for the single live-test validator (full drain); wait for the ack and the callback (Validators tab: its recorded delegation drops to zero; Funds tab: its bar moves to unbonding). The tx refuses the zone while any record is queued or retrying (Funds tab → Records).

echo '[{"address": "<LIVE_TEST_VALOPER>", "offset": "0"}]' > /tmp/live-test-<CHAIN_ID>.json
strided tx stakeibc undelegate-from-validators <CHAIN_ID> /tmp/live-test-<CHAIN_ID>.json --from <PROTOCOL_ADMIN_KEY> --chain-id stride-1 --node https://stride-strd-rpc.polkachu.com:443 --gas 12000000
steps.expect: Gas: about 9M is a fixed cost (the queued-record guard reads every epoch unbonding record), so set --gas explicitly; 12M covers a one-validator drain on every zone. code: 0 and the ICA acks (Channels tab: the zone's DELEGATION channel back to 0 pending acks; Validators tab: the validator's recorded delegation drops to 0 and its Δ in progress back to 0). A rejection before submission names the reason (a queued or retrying record, a validator with a change or slash query in progress, a deprecated zone): resolve it, do not force. An ack error leaves the delegation unchanged: look at the host tx log for the validator the host rejected.

steps.text: Per zone: MsgUndelegateFromValidators with an empty validator list for the rest; relay acks before timeouts; wait for every batch to ack. A failed batch (a slash since the refresh): rerun the refresh or set that validator's offset and resubmit the affected validators.

The Hub's 15 acks cost about 1.5M each, so a relayer packing them into one tx needs about 22M. code: 0, then every batch acks (Channels tab: 0 pending on the DELEGATION channel; Validators tab: recorded delegations at dust, Δ in progress 0; Funds tab: the zone's bar is all Unbonding). A failed batch (ack error) means a validator moved since the refresh: rerun update-delegation for it, or resubmit the batch's validators with a file and an offset, within the 19:00–08:00 UTC window.

steps.text: If a validator was drained with an offset, run CalibrateDelegation on it afterwards to zero the leftover recorded amount; a validator with a stale SlashQueryInProgress is corrected by CalibrateDelegation, not by an offset.

steps.expect: code: 0; after the callback the Validators tab shows the validator's recorded delegation equal to the host's (zero after a full drain).

avoid: Do not relay timeouts for haqq packets 85-98 (§9 step 1c).

days.title: Last days: the sweep
avoid: Vouchers over the four hosts outside SweepUnwindChannels (phoenix-1, laozi-mainnet, injective-1, haqq_11235-1) are never swept; they are announced as self-service (§7).
Do not stop a transfer-channel relayer while any packet or acknowledgement is outstanding in either direction (§9 step 9).

Once a foreign-route pool has received its full allocation, do not fund it again: native paid out through redemptions is never replenished, and the halt check compares the deposits to the allocation (§8 Funding, §9 halt checklist).

steps.text: Fresh strided export; build the batches with scripts/wind-down/build_sweep_batches.py at the announced floor: every holder at or above it, every denom on the sweep list (eleven stTokens and ustrd to Osmosis, whitelisted vouchers back one hop).
steps.command: python3 scripts/wind-down/build_sweep_batches.py --export export.json --prices prices.json --denoms stuatom,stuosmo,stutia,stinj,stadydx,staISLM,stujuno,stuband,stuluna,stusomm,stusaga,ustrd --floor-usd <FLOOR> --out-dir sweep-batches --as-of <BLOCK_TIME_OF_EXPORT> [--extra-denom ibc/...=<price>:<decimals>] [--batch-size 100]
steps.expect: RESULT: DONE with the holder count, batch-file count and USD total. Fill in the export (strided export at the chosen height), prices.json, the announced floor and --as-of (the block time at the export height, from strided q block <height>). Each file under sweep-batches/ is one tx for the next step. A non-zero exit names the input that is malformed. The export: `strided export --output-document <file>` on a stopped node or a copy of its data (on SDK 0.54 a bare `strided export` writes nothing to stdout); then trim per app/upgrades/v35/testdata/README.md.

steps.text: MsgSweepTokensOffStride batches (sweep operator; up to 100 addresses each or the size from the gas measurement); watch num_skipped and the skip events; resubmit any address whose transfer timed out (its balance is back on Stride).
steps.command: strided tx stakeibc sweep-tokens-off-stride <DENOMS> sweep-batches/<FILE> --from <SWEEP_OPERATOR_KEY> ...
steps.expect: One tx per batch file; the response's num_skipped and the skip events say which addresses the chain refused (module accounts, ICAs, contracts): expected to be zero for a batch the builder produced. A transfer error (closed channel) rejects the whole tx; a timeout refunds that holder on Stride: resubmit its address.

steps.text: Relayers on channel-5 and on every whitelisted channel (channel-0, -162, -24, -150, -213, -160) up until the last sweep packet acks.

After the holder sweeps: the F5 multisig moves the community pool off Stride by hand. The v35 handler sent the pool to stride1k8c2m5cn322akk5wy8lpt87dd2f4yh9azg7jlh, which the batch builder leaves out (BUILDER_EXCLUDED_ADDRESSES). First spend what has accrued in the pool since the upgrade to F5 with MsgCommunityPoolSpend (F5 signs as the chain authority; with no bonded validators the staking share of fees goes to the pool every block), then IBC-transfer F5's balances out: stTokens and ustrd over channel-5 to the Osmosis vault osmo1k8c2m5cn322akk5wy8lpt87dd2f4yh9afcd7af, whitelisted vouchers back over their own channel.
steps.command: strided q distribution community-pool --node https://stride-strd-rpc.polkachu.com:443 && strided q bank balances stride1k8c2m5cn322akk5wy8lpt87dd2f4yh9azg7jlh --node https://stride-strd-rpc.polkachu.com:443
steps.expect: Before: the pool's refill since the upgrade and F5's balances, which set the amounts to spend and transfer. After: the pool holds only sub-unit dust plus whatever accrued since the spend, and F5 keeps only what it needs for fees until the halt.

steps.text: Announce: the sweep is done; holders below the floor and holders of non-whitelisted vouchers move themselves; nobody should send funds to Stride near or after the halt (late inbound packets may be unrecoverable).

Validators and STRD delegators withdraw their rewards and commission (including stTokens, which they move to Osmosis themselves); the interchain-account and 32-byte holders notified on 10-02 reminded one last time.

days.title: Halt
days.note: Every bullet of the halt checklist, then the halt-height.
avoid: Do not assume a packet left toward the halted chain will refund; clear both directions first (§9 halt checklist).

steps.text: Funds tab → every zone's Transfer checklist ready and Records column at 0 / 0: zero stakeibc user redemption records, zero HostZoneUnbonding records outside CLAIMABLE with a non-zero amount, no claim pending; celestia's staketia line ready (zero unbonding records outside CLAIMED, zero redemption records) and the claim address drained (accounts table).
Validators tab: no validator with Δ in progress, recorded at dust on every zone; Funds tab: TotalDelegations at dust except celestia's multisig portion.
All four ICA balances at dust on every zone (Funds tab). Celestia multisig delegation zero, its unbondings complete, its balance on Osmosis.
Every pool, canonical and per route, created, funded, marked one-way, and passing scripts/wind-down/coverage_check.py against a fresh export. Publish the output.
steps.command:
python3 scripts/wind-down/coverage_check.py --export export.json.gz --pools pools.json --vault osmo1k8c2m5cn322akk5wy8lpt87dd2f4yh9afcd7af
python3 scripts/wind-down/check_transmuter_pool.py --funded
steps.expect: Both RESULT: PASS against a fresh export; publish the coverage output. Any FAIL blocks the halt. The export: `strided export --output-document <file>` on a stopped node or a copy of its data (on SDK 0.54 a bare `strided export` writes nothing to stdout); then trim per app/upgrades/v35/testdata/README.md.

steps.text: For each foreign-route pool, the native funding deposits (including any test deposit) total exactly its allocation; check the deposits, not the remaining balance; no redemption payout replenished.
No sweepable account at or above the floor holds any in-scope stToken, ustrd or a whitelisted voucher; no sweep packet outstanding on channel-5 or a whitelisted channel.
Channels tab: every channel used in the ops window shows 0 pending packets and 0 pending acks in both directions, including inbound transfers to Stride; nothing stuck.
Validators and STRD delegators have withdrawn their rewards; interchain-account holders notified.
Transfer-channel relayers stopped only after the clearing check; ICA channels left to close.
Validators set the halt-height and the chain stops.

days.title: After the halt
avoid: No relayer updates Osmosis's light client of Stride (07-tendermint-2119) after the halt (§9 step 10).

steps.text: Every validator rotates or destroys its consensus key and Stride Labs confirms it in writing from each (closes the forged-header window on Osmosis's client on day 0 rather than day 12).
A holder with a third-hop stToken denom asks for a pool: create one the same way, funded by moving native tokens out of the canonical pool; add_new_assets is otherwise not used.
Pools outlive the chain; the vault keeps the alloyed receipts; reclaiming unclaimed backing by exiting the pools is a later policy decision.
